fire_sequence: ROTATION fire. Read the module's full falsification-ledger history (30 prior amphora-molecule-property entries, 2026-08-01 through 2026-08-18) and cross-referenced against evidence/phase0/kpis/ RETRACTION-INDEX.md (the R-A09 completeness sweep, 2026-08-03). Found several KPIs marked STANDS with 'none - no refuting receipt targets this KPI'; the van-krevelen-tg-*-15-canonical-homopolymers and van-krevelen-ridge-retuned-Ygi KPIs are already honest negative findings (R2<0, MAE worse than published baselines -- nothing confident to falsify). polyuniverse-epoxy-tg-external-validation-5-canonical-epoxy-amines-kpi.v1.json is the strongest still-standing POSITIVE claim never ledger-attacked: 'ML MAE 39.1C beats Van Krevelen physical baseline MAE 109.1C by 70.0C' on 5 canonical DGEBA epoxy-amine hardeners (IPDA/m-XDA/DDS/TETA/DETA), the exact in-scope coating chemistry class for this portfolio, and it is the origin receipt for the module-wide Polyuniverse-Epoxy units correction (heavily cited downstream, e.g. by W12 and the coating-candidate-design-card KPI). Every MAE gate in sibling KPIs across this module carries an explicit NULL-median/mean baseline comparison EXCEPT this one's 'ml_beats_van_krevelen_physical_baseline_on_MAE' and 'ml_MAE_less_than_50C_across_5_external_candidates' gates, whose note frames MAE<50C as 'useful engineering Tg prediction'. Both models produce near-degenerate near-constant predictions on the 5 candidates (VK spread 0.6C -- a known +250C-offset bug already disclosed in this module's own van-krevelen-tg-external-validation-15-canonical-homopolymers KPI; ML spread 23.4C, also narrow vs the actual 120C spread of published values), which is exactly the pattern where 'beats a known-bad baseline' can mask 'beaten by a baseline that ignores structure entirely' -- the same asymmetry that made W13's majority-baseline audit (2026-08-18) fire on a different KPI in this module.
method: Independently re-verified the pinned Epoxy_1M_p.csv (repo-relative feedback/v1/external_data/polyuniverse_epoxy/raw/Epoxy_1M_p.csv) against its sha256 pin shared by the KPI under attack (9f1f5c593463b9c26a026948901e37b4db545d17f05d5cd80baca5c3e14e0c45), read literally in the module's own already-disclosed unit correction (degrees C, not K), and computed the full 1,000,000-row population mean and median Tg. Transcribed the 5 per-candidate published Tg values and ML/VK predictions verbatim from the scientific receipt under attack (reference/mvp20/data/polyuniverse_epoxy_tg_external_validation_5_canonical_epoxy_amines_receipt.v1.json) and reproduced the receipt's own headline ml_MAE_C=39.11947866164949 and vk_MAE_C=109.07781373364219 bit-for-bit as a fidelity check before computing anything new. Built two structure-blind null baselines (constant population mean, constant population median) plus one internal leave-one-out-of-the-5-actuals control, and compared their MAE against the ML model's MAE on the identical 5 candidates.

leave_one_out_mean_of_other_4_actuals.note: Non-circular internal control using only the 5-candidate test set itself; NOT the primary refutation criterion (population-mean/median are), reported for robustness.

objective: Test whether 'ML MAE 39.1C beats Van Krevelen physics MAE 109.1C by 70.0C' on the 5 canonical epoxy-amine external-validation set reflects genuine ML predictive skill, or is fully explained by Van Krevelen's own known offset-degeneracy bug being a uniquely bad comparison point -- i.e. whether a trivial, zero-structural-information constant-value predictor also beats the ML model on the identical 5 candidates.
pre_registered_refute_criterion: The claim that ML MAE=39.12C on this 5-candidate set demonstrates real predictive skill (as opposed to an artifact of comparison against an unusually degenerate physics baseline) is REFUTED if EITHER: (a) a trivial constant-value baseline -- predicting the full Polyuniverse Epoxy 1M raw population MEAN Tg for all 5 candidates, using zero molecular/structural information -- achieves MAE <= ML's observed MAE (39.11947866164949 C); OR (b) the same constant-value baseline using the population MEDIAN achieves MAE <= ML's observed MAE. Both criteria were fixed before computing the null baseline; both use only the already-pinned Epoxy_1M_p.csv, so this attacks whether the ML-vs-VK COMPARISON is informative, not whether the ML model was correctly trained.

prediction_degeneracy.note: VK spread of 0.6C across 5 structurally distinct amines confirms the near-pure +250C-offset degenerate-output bug already disclosed in this module's van-krevelen-tg-external-validation-15-canonical-homopolymers-kpi.v1.json. ML spread of 23.4C is also narrow relative to the actual 120C spread of published values (100-220C).

scope_note: This does not re-attack or alter the applicability-domain gate (4/5 LOW-AD flag, already independently confirmed correct behavior) or the units-correction disclosure (both untouched, both remain accurate). It is scoped to exactly two things: (1) the 'ml_beats_van_krevelen_physical_baseline_on_MAE' gate and its 'usable Tg predictions' framing in docs/mission.md, both of which compare ML only against Van Krevelen physics and never against a structure-blind null; and (2) the 'ml_MAE_less_than_50C_across_5_external_candidates' gate's note text asserting this represents 'useful engineering Tg prediction'.
why: Fidelity check: independently reproduced the receipt's own headline numbers bit-for-bit (ml_MAE_C=39.11947866164949, vk_MAE_C=109.07781373364216), confirming this attack targets the correct, real published numbers. The pinned Epoxy_1M_p.csv (n=1000000 rows, hash-verified) has population mean Tg=118.1848 C and median=117.5982 C. A trivial constant predictor that always outputs the population mean (zero structural information, no scaffold split, no training) achieves MAE=32.9630 C on the SAME 5 candidates -- LOWER than the ML model's own MAE of 39.1195 C. The population-median constant predictor achieves MAE=33.0804 C, also lower than ML. Both pre-registered refutation criteria fired (criterion_a=True, criterion_b=True). This does not mean the ML model has literally zero skill -- its MAE (39.1C) is closer to the null-mean MAE (33.0C) than VK's MAE (109.1C) is -- but it means the module's own headline framing ('ML beats Van Krevelen physics by 70C' as evidence the model gives 'usable' Tg predictions on canonical industrial hardeners) is not supported by comparison to any informative baseline: the single most obvious sanity-check predictor, which uses no chemistry at all, beats the machine-learning model outright on this exact 5-candidate population. The degeneracy analysis shows why both models look artificially good/bad relative to each other: VK's predictions span only 0.6C across 5 structurally distinct amines (a near-pure +250C offset, a bug independently documented in this module's van-krevelen-tg-external-validation-15-canonical-homopolymers-kpi.v1.json), so 'beating VK' mostly measures how badly broken VK's offset term is here, not how good the ML predictions are.
